nodes.title: the Keldmux signature
nodes.statement: The Keldmux system concerns objects called thrafexs. There are exactly 3 of them: tuespa, qenmorn, hobzel. Two operations are written =| and ~. One relation is written =<, read as "supports".

nodes.title: the Keldmux combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x =| y for every pair of thrafexs is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for ~. The pairs standing in the =< relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x and y, x =| y is again a thrafex.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x, y, z: (x =| y) =| z = x =| (y =| z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x and y: x =| y = y =| x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a thrafex tuespa with tuespa =| x = x =| tuespa = x for every x.

nodes.title: reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: For every thrafex x there is a thrafex y with x =| y = y =| x = tuespa.

nodes.title: cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x, y, z: if x =| y = x =| z then y = z.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x and y, x ~ y is again a thrafex.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x, y, z: (x ~ y) ~ z = x ~ (y ~ z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x and y: x ~ y = y ~ x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a thrafex tuespa with tuespa ~ x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every thrafex x: x ~ x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every thrafex x: x =< x.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x, y, z: if x =< y and y =< z then x =< z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x and y, at least one of x =< y and y =< x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x, y, z: if x =< y then (z =| x) =< (z =| y) and (x =| z) =< (y =| z).

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all thrafexs x, y, z: if x =< y then (z ~ x) =< (z ~ y) and (x ~ z) =< (y ~ z).

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every thrafex x: x =| x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = qenmorn, value = hobzel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is no thrafex z with z =| x = x =| z = z for every thrafex x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case reason = no absorbing element, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have spreading of the second operation over the first
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all thrafexs x, y, z: x ~ (y =| z) = (x ~ y) =| (x ~ z), and the same on the right.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = qenmorn, y = tuespa, z = tuespa, left = qenmorn, right = hobzel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have the absorption pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all thrafexs x and y: x =| (x ~ y) = x and x ~ (x =| y) = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = tuespa, y = qenmorn, value = qenmorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all thrafexs x and y: if x =< y and y =< x then x = y.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = tuespa, y = qenmorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: solka thrafexs
nodes.statement: A thrafex x is called solka when x =| x = x.

nodes.title: thrafexs that tutez
nodes.statement: Two thrafexs x and y are said to tutez when x =| y = y =| x.

nodes.title: umbbra collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of thrafexs is umbbra when x =| y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the vextarn of a thrafex
nodes.statement: The vextarn of a thrafex x is the collection of thrafexs y for which x =< y holds.

nodes.title: the nyrrast
nodes.statement: The thrafex tuespa is called the nyrrast of the system. It is the unique thrafex that leaves every thrafex unchanged under =|.

nodes.title: the aztrast
nodes.statement: The aztrast of the system is the collection of thrafexs that tutez with every thrafex.

nodes.title: the tumux
nodes.statement: The tumux is the collection of all solka thrafexs.

nodes.title: the muxmi of a thrafex
nodes.statement: The muxmi of a thrafex x, written [x], is the smallest umbbra collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a ponjen
nodes.statement: A thrafex f is a ponjen when f =< y holds for every thrafex y, that is, when the vextarn of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: iskrast thrafexs
nodes.statement: A thrafex x is iskrast when x =| x equals the nyrrast.

nodes.title: the nyrzel of a thrafex
nodes.statement: A nyrzel of a thrafex x is a thrafex y with x =| y = y =| x = tuespa.

nodes.title: the driglim of a thrafex
nodes.statement: The driglim of a thrafex x is the number of thrafexs in its muxmi [x].

nodes.title: the reldumb
nodes.statement: The reldumb of the system is the collection of thrafexs whose driglim is largest.

nodes.title: falkeld pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct thrafexs x and y form a falkeld pair when x =< y and y =< x both hold, that is, when each lies in the vextarn of the other.

nodes.title: the nyrrast is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one thrafex e with e =| x = x =| e = x for every thrafex x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every thrafex unchanged.
Then e =| f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e =| f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the nyrrast lies in the aztrast
nodes.statement: The nyrrast tutezs with every thrafex.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the nyrrast and x any thrafex.
Then e =| x = x and x =| e = x.
So e =| x = x =| e, which is what it means to tutez.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the aztrast.

nodes.title: a thrafex has only one nyrzel
nodes.statement: For every thrafex x there is exactly one nyrzel of x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y and z both be partners of x.
Then y = y =| (x =| z) = (y =| x) =| z.
Both bracketed products collapse to the neutral object.
So y = z.

nodes.title: a iskrast thrafex is its own nyrzel
nodes.statement: If x =| x is the nyrrast then the nyrzel of x is x itself.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x be iskrast, so x =| x is the nyrrast.
That is exactly the condition for x to be a partner of x.
Partners are unique, so no other object can be one.

nodes.title: the aztrast is umbbra
nodes.statement: If x and y both tutez with every thrafex, then so does x =| y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the aztrast and let z be any thrafex.
Then (x =| y) =| z = x =| (y =| z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each tutezs with everything.
So x =| y tutezs with z, and the aztrast is umbbra.

nodes.title: the muxmi of a thrafex is umbbra
nodes.statement: For every thrafex x, the collection [x] is umbbra.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under =|.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the muxmi is contained in every umbbra collection
nodes.statement: If S is umbbra and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a thrafex is solka exactly when its driglim is one
nodes.statement: x =| x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x =| x = x then {x} is already closed under =|.
So [x] = {x} and the driglim is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x =| x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the driglim divides the number of thrafexs
nodes.statement: For every thrafex x, the driglim of x divides 3.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a umbbra collection.
Its size is the driglim of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 3.

nodes.title: the muxmi of a aztrast thrafex stays in the aztrast
nodes.statement: If x lies in the aztrast then every thrafex of [x] lies in the aztrast.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The aztrast is umbbra.
[x] is the smallest umbbra collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the aztrast is one.

nodes.title: the tumux is umbbra
nodes.statement: If x and y are both solka then so is x =| y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be solka.
The claim asks whether (x =| y) =| (x =| y) returns x =| y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: combining on the left never merges two thrafexs
nodes.statement: For every thrafex a, the assignment x to a =| x sends distinct thrafexs to distinct thrafexs.

verification.domain: every object translated by every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose a =| x = a =| y.
Cancellation on the left gives x = y.
So the assignment is injective, and being injective on a finite carrier it is onto.

nodes.title: vextarns are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the vextarn of x, then the vextarn of y is contained in the vextarn of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x =< y and let z satisfy y =< z.
Transitivity gives x =< z.
So every member of the vextarn of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: the system has a ponjen
nodes.statement: Some thrafex ponjens the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x =< y then (x =| z) =< (y =| z) for every thrafex z.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the vextarn of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: every thrafex lies in the aztrast
nodes.statement: Every pair of thrafexs tutezs.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The aztrast is defined by tutezing with everything.
The claim is that x =| y = y =| x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every thrafex is solka breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x =| x = x for every thrafex x.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = qenmorn, value = hobzel, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: some thrafex reaches every other
nodes.statement: There is a thrafex whose muxmi is the whole system.

verification.domain: every object and its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Compute [x] for each thrafex in turn.
The claim is that some driglim equals 3.
The search runs over finitely many objects, so it settles.

nodes.title: the relation reads the same in both directions
nodes.statement: If x =< y then y =< x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Symmetry would mean y lies in the vextarn of x exactly when x lies in that of y.
The listed pairs settle it directly.

nodes.title: where the nyrrast swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e =| x equals the nyrrast for every thrafex x.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = tuespa, x = qenmorn, value = qenmorn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the aztrast intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the aztrast then so does x ~ y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The aztrast is already umbbra under =|.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that ~ respects the aztrast as well.
